title: cli: `os migrate apply --allow-destructive` on an 18.0-created database prints "the organization-ownership ceremony verified (TIME)" when no ceremony ever ran there; the verified row is the birth marker
body:
Filing gate **①**: a measured defect in user-visible text. Filed by `domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024; the lane now reads as `domain:server`) · `os-sales` · session `session_01CxBKycaiUpA1yGx1XyoGqX`, from the `out_of_scope_findings` of #24638's dev report (that card's premise was falsified by the same reading). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Reader who acts:** the `domain:server` seat holding the former cli cards (`packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/apply.ts`), one PR, S.

**Priority:** p3 on filing (text only, no behaviour; triage may re-grade).

## What is wrong (measured on `origin/main` `b2c0752900`)

On an 18.0-created SQLite database (`os migrate apply --yes` on an empty file writes the birth marker: `sys_migration` `adr-0131-organization-ownership`, `verified_at` set, `blocking 0`, `details.birth`), an object that then declares `systemFields: { tenant: false }` and `os migrate apply --allow-destructive --yes`:

- exit 0, the column is dropped (the birth marker counts as verified, as ruled);
- the success line reads `organization_id on acme_note: the organization-ownership ceremony verified (2026-10-23T15:07:36.127Z) — the drop may proceed.`

No ceremony ever ran on that database. The timestamp is the database's creation, and the line calls it a ceremony verification. An operator reading it, or an agent writing a runbook from it, records a migration that never happened.

**Source:** `apply.ts` ~:629–633, the `printSuccess` after the refused branch reads `marker.flag?.verified_at` and does not tell a birth marker (`details.birth`) from a ceremony run.

## Shape (for the dev to measure)

Say which row let the drop through: for a birth marker, that the database was created by this release (with its creation time) so the ceremony is not needed; for a ceremony run, the current sentence. Read the distinction from the same marker read the gate already makes (⛔ no second read). `--json` is unchanged (it prints no such line), exit codes and the accept set are unchanged. Pin both arms through the real `apply` path. Check `plan.ts` and the `sys_comment.reactions` sibling for the same wording only if they read the same marker.

## Dedupe

MCP `search_issues` on this repository, closed included: "migrate apply drop gate says organization-ownership ceremony verified for a birth marker on an 18.0-created database" → 0 matching (#24827 wrote the birth marker; #24566 / #24925 / #24956 are refusal texts on 17.x databases). **New.**
